A conceptual diagram illustrating the causes of African discontent. In the center is a large circle titled "African Discontent". Pointing into it are three large arrows. Arrow 1 (Political): "Loss of sovereignty, exclusion of elites, harsh laws like indigénat". Arrow 2 (Economic): "Land alienation, heavy taxation, forced labour, low prices for cash crops". Arrow 3 (Social): "Racial discrimination, poor education, separate settlements".

An illustration showing returning African soldiers after World War II. In the foreground, two African soldiers in British military uniforms (slouch hats, khaki shorts) are stepping off a ship's gangway, greeted by a crowd of cheering African civilians. One civilian in traditional attire is holding up a newspaper with the bold headline "ATLANTIC CHARTER: SELF-DETERMINATION". The mood is energetic and determined.

A map of Africa in the 1960s/70s. Different colors distinguish how countries achieved independence. Countries in West Africa (Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal, Ivory Coast) are shaded light blue with a legend key reading "Constitutional/Peaceful Process". Countries like Algeria, Kenya, Angola, Mozambique, and Zimbabwe are shaded dark red with a legend key reading "Armed Struggle / Guerrilla War".
